stories.headline: Dow soars 1,569 points for best day since April 2025 on Democratic midterm sweep
stories.summary: The Dow rose 3.03% to 53,356.12, the S&P 500 1.58% to 7,688.62 and the Nasdaq 1.44% to 25,736.51 as Trump accepted the results, oil plunged more than 8%, and investors bet divided government is good for stocks.

breadth.label: Percent of S&P 500 stocks above 50-day MA
breadth.note: Below 30 bullish, above 70 bearish. Computed by Thaddeus from Yahoo Finance daily closes for 501 of 503 current S&P 500 constituents at the Nov. 4 close (mimics MMFI). Breadth jumped with Wednesday's broad midterm-relief rally even as AI names lagged.

fear_greed.commentary: Fear & Greed held at 27 (fear) after Wednesday's close, flat with the prior close and down from 31 a week ago and 43 a month ago, so the midterm rally has not yet thawed sentiment.

markets.summary: A midterm relief rally lifted the Dow 3.03% to 53,356.12 — its best day since April 2025 — while the S&P 500 rose 1.58% to 7,688.62 and the Nasdaq 1.44% to 25,736.51 after Democrats took Congress and President Trump accepted the results; oil's sharp drop and hopes for gridlock fueled the advance. Tech split: Mag-7 names such as Apple, Amazon and Microsoft surged, but AI infrastructure stocks sold off on Texas data-center-moratorium fears, with Nvidia down 3.17% to $200.13 (still below its 40-week average, RSI 34.5). Small caps joined the bounce, the Russell 2000 up 1.58% to 2,856.95 and above its 40-week average. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.89%, down roughly 1.17% on the day and still up about 18% year to date. Gold futures rose 1.32% to about $4,127 and silver futures 0.81% to about $52.54; both remain below their 40-week averages, with silver still down about 25% year to date.

stories.headline: SpaceX and Tesla fall as Democrats sweep midterms and Texas
stories.summary: SPCX closed down 3.8% at $135.92 as investors weighed Democratic control of Congress and Gina Hinojosa's Texas governor win, which raises the risk of a data-center moratorium in a state that hosts SpaceX and a large share of planned U.S. AI capacity.

stories.headline: SpaceX slides as $40B chip financing hits the market and political heat rises
stories.summary: Shares also faced pressure as Goldman and Apollo reportedly shopped slices of SpaceX's $40 billion Nvidia-equipment financing, while Sen. Ted Cruz warned Democrats may use subpoenas against Elon Musk.

stories.headline: Cameco says Westinghouse reactor builds could outgrow mining by 2030
stories.summary: COO Grant Isaac told The Northern Miner that Westinghouse's new-reactor pipeline could contribute more to Cameco's growth by 2030 than uranium mining if key projects reach FID; CCJ still closed down 1.2% at $71.68, extending its post-Q3 slide.

stories.headline: Nvidia drops 3% as AI data-center stocks sell off after Democratic sweep
stories.summary: NVDA closed at $200.13 amid fears that Democratic wins — especially in Texas, where the new governor backs a data-center moratorium — could slow AI infrastructure buildout; Mag-7 peers mostly rose while semiconductors and neoclouds fell.

headlines.headline: AI data-center stocks slide as Texas governor result raises buildout risks
headlines.summary: SpaceX, Nvidia and neocloud names fell even as the broader market rallied, after Democrat Gina Hinojosa won Texas and pledged an immediate moratorium on data centers in a state that holds about 27% of planned U.S. gigawatts.

stories.headline: Douglas County voters expand the county commission from three members to five
stories.summary: Voters approved growing the Board of County Commissioners to five seats, starting a transition that could change how DougCo is governed and how commissioners are elected, though some details remain unclear.

weather.summary: Heavy snow winds down in the central Rockies early Thursday as a weak front moves east, bringing rain to the central and southern Plains and showers and storms from the Ohio Valley to the central Gulf Coast. Rain spreads from the Appalachians into the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic Thursday, light snow reaches Michigan's Upper Peninsula Thursday night, and the Pacific Northwest sees light rain and mountain snow.
